# Architecture Document Rules

Scope: `docs/architecture/**` — ADRs, the TR registry, the control manifest, the
traceability matrix, and every doc derived from them.

Owning agent: `technical-director`.

## ⚠️ Resolve every ID before you cite it

**An ID written into prose is a claim that the ID exists.** A `TR-` or `ADR-`
token that does not resolve is worse than a missing citation: it looks
authoritative, it survives review, and downstream docs copy it. Every phantom ID
found in this project so far was invented by a doc that restated a requirement
instead of looking it up.

**Rule: no `TR-` token may appear in any file under `docs/architecture/**`
unless it resolves verbatim in `docs/architecture/tr-registry.yaml`.** Check
before the doc is considered done, not at audit time.

```bash
# 1. Every TR token cited anywhere under docs/architecture/, minus those the
#    registry actually defines. Output MUST be empty.
comm -23 \
  <(grep -rhoE "TR-[a-z]+-[0-9]{3}" docs/architecture/ --include=*.md | sort -u) \
  <(grep -oE "^  - id: (TR-[a-z]+-[0-9]{3})$" docs/architecture/tr-registry.yaml \
      | sed 's/^  - id: //' | sort -u)

# 2. Single-ID spot check while writing — must print 1, never 0.
grep -c "id: TR-combat-012" docs/architecture/tr-registry.yaml
```

- **The system slug must be one of the ten the registry defines**: `camp`,
  `combat`, `core`, `defence`, `economy`, `mechanics`, `meta`, `raid`, `audio`,
  `ui` (`audio` added 2026-08-24, `ui` added 2026-09-02 by ADR-035). Inventing
  a slug produces an ID that can never resolve — `TR-sim-001` is the live
  example, and there has never been a `sim` slug.
- **Never restate a requirement's text.** Copy it from the registry entry, or
  reference the ID and let the registry hold the wording. A near-verbatim
  restatement is how `TR-combat-016`/`-017` came to duplicate `TR-combat-012`/
  `-014` and be double-counted as gaps.
- **Never allocate a TR-ID yourself.** IDs are "highest existing + 1" with no
  reservation, so two agents will collide. `docs/architecture/tr-registry.yaml`
  is lead-only; report the entry and let the lead add it. IDs are permanent —
  never renumber, never delete (use `status: deprecated` or `superseded-by`).
- The same discipline applies to **`ADR-NNN` citations**: the file must exist in
  `docs/architecture/` and the section named must exist inside it. Cross-check
  the topic, not just the number — an ADR number that resolves to the wrong
  subject is still a wrong citation.

  ```bash
  # Every ADR number cited under docs/architecture/ and src/ must have a file.
  grep -rhoE "ADR-[0-9]{3}" docs/architecture/ src/ --include=*.md --include=*.cs \
    | sort -u | while read id; do
        ls docs/architecture/${id}-*.md >/dev/null 2>&1 || echo "UNRESOLVED: $id"
      done
  ```

## Derived documents are not sources

`requirements-traceability.md`, gap analyses, review reports and sprint
summaries are **derived**. They restate what the registry and the ADRs hold, and
they rot silently.

- Resolve every ID in a derived doc against the authoritative file before
  restating it.
- **Never trust a stated count.** A "Total: N requirements" or "9 canonical
  sections" line drifts from the rows beneath it. Re-derive counts from the
  entries on disk every time — this has been caught four separate times in this
  project.
- A previous gate verdict of "current" or "fresh" is a snapshot, not a
  guarantee. Diff against disk before restating it.

## ADR structure

Template: `.claude/docs/templates/architecture-decision-record.md`.

Required sections: Title, Status, Context, Decision, Consequences, ADR
Dependencies, Engine Compatibility, GDD Requirements Addressed.

- Status lifecycle: `Proposed` → `Accepted` → `Superseded`. Never skip
  `Accepted` — stories referencing a `Proposed` ADR are auto-blocked.
- Filename: `ADR-NNN-kebab-slug.md`, three-digit zero-padded, allocated by the
  lead.
- **Performance Implications must carry numbers**, checked against the budgets
  in `.claude/docs/technical-preferences.md` (60 fps / 16.6 ms / ≤120 draw calls
  / ≤400 MB / <50 ms counterfactual re-run). "Should be fine" is not an analysis.
- **Alternatives Considered must name what was rejected and why.** An ADR with
  one option is a record of a decision nobody made.

## Control manifest

`docs/architecture/control-manifest.md` carries a date-stamped `Manifest
Version:` in its header. Stories embed that version and `/story-done` checks it
for staleness — so any change to the manifest bumps the version in the same
edit.
